title: How the farm reads through the walls
question:
**Pick how the live farm should look beyond an interior's walls. Recommendation: draw it unchanged.**

P-18 settled the geometry on 2026-09-15: one world, one metric, two grids. A building's interior is a finer grid nested inside the building's footprint, and going inside is a uniform camera zoom of x2. Nothing stretches or moves independently.

The new comparison puts both the farmhouse and the coop between ripe wheat and tomatoes on one side, and fencing and a hen on the other. Each building keeps the same room, yard and framing across all four rows; only the treatment changes. The rooms and yard are assembled from the game's shipped art at the sizes the x2 camera draws them. The coop interior does not exist in the running game yet, so these are controlled mockups rather than screenshots.

At this scale the room itself already says that the player is inside. Leaving the yard unchanged keeps the crop, fence and hen easiest to read. Haze adds a strong checker over the things the player needs to notice; darkening loses the crop first; and the hard-cut wall keeps the yard clear but spends much more of the view on a frame. Pick the stronger separation only if the unchanged yard still feels like the world came closer rather than a view outside.
why_now: The geometry is settled, so Daniel can judge the remaining visual treatment against the same house and coop staging. Options (a), (b), and (c) use the existing yard with no treatment or an added dither or colour layer. Option (d) would need new solid wall art for a finished game implementation; its frame here is only a placeholder made from the current wall tile.

options.label: Nothing at all (Recommended)
options.detail: Draw the yard exactly as it is drawn outdoors, only twice the size. The room already supplies the indoor cue, while the ripe plants, fence and hen stay clearest. It is also the only option with no new visual layer or wall art.

options.label: Haze
options.detail: An ordered dither of one pale colour over everything beyond the walls, on the art's own pixel grid — the studio's existing vocabulary for a soft edge, no blur. Says 'through a window' without hiding the hen.

options.label: Desaturate and darken
options.detail: Keep every pixel but drain the yard towards grey and down a step in value, so the room is the lit thing. Reads as an interior most strongly; the price is that a crow out there is harder to notice, which is one of the reasons for seeing out.

options.label: Hard-cut walls, clear yard
options.detail: No treatment on the yard at all, but the walls draw as a solid opaque frame that bites into it, so what you see out is framed rather than faded. The window metaphor made literal; costs wall art the game does not have yet.

attachments.caption: Four treatments with unchanged staging in each column: farmhouse left, coop right, with ripe wheat and tomatoes, fencing and a hen beside them. A controlled mockup composed from current sprite art at x2 camera scale. The coop interior is not yet a gameplay capture; the hard-cut frame uses a repeated wall tile to stand in for new art.
The two zooms. Left: the house on its three tiles by two, the room inside at half pitch. Right: x2, and nothing has moved. Both the same photograph of the game.

replies.text:
Checked, and the answer is in two parts.

**What the session settled and what it did not.** The geometry is settled (P-18, 2026-09-15: one world, one metric, two grids) and the yard seen through the walls is the live farm since 2026-09-16 (commit a15cc5e). That shipped with option (a), nothing at all, as the placeholder. The look — haze, desaturate, hard-cut — was never ruled, and the decision log says why: nothing had been seen. So this card is not closed by that work; it is smaller. It comes back to you as four captures of the real room, one per treatment, to pick from, and Sam is shooting them. Nothing needs you until they exist.

**Other stories in the same boat.** Nine cards were waiting for your verdict on work that has been on main since 10–11 September: the four Animation Lab waves (the loops as sheets, the crow morning, the robot's ladder, the story-night frame) and four workbench cards filed off Q-101. Eight are closed today under the new rule that landed work needs no verdict (S-16); the ninth, the overnight loop, is held open by another session mid-edit and closes when it is free.

The card now shows both the farmhouse and coop under all four treatments, each beside ripe wheat and tomatoes, fencing, and a hen. The staging stays fixed within each building column, so the changed treatment is visible without moving the scene. These are controlled mockups using the game's current sprites at x2 camera scale. The coop interior is not built in the running game yet, and the hard-cut frame is a placeholder for wall art that would need to be made.

I recommend leaving the yard unchanged: the room already shows that the player is inside, and the crop, fence and hen retain their full contrast. If the frame itself should create a stronger indoor feeling, hard-cut walls preserve a clear yard but require new art and hide more of the scene. Which treatment should the game use beyond the house and coop walls?
